assumptions: Finite-dimensional n-qubit Pauli stabilizer code; each chosen generator is a signed Hermitian Pauli operator with g_i^2=I.
The generators commute and their generated group S excludes -I, so the simultaneous +1 eigenspace is nonzero.
The state vector is a nonzero code vector. Fixing any generating set is equivalent to fixing every group element; the displayed quantifier ranges over all of S.
variables: S: Abelian subgroup of the n-qubit Pauli group excluding -I; g_i: an element or selected generator of S.
|psi>: vector in the common +1 eigenspace; r: number of independent generators if a generating set is counted.
patches.regime: Defines the code subspace. A unique pure stabilizer state up to phase requires r=n independent generators; r<n describes an encoded subspace rather than a unique state. No claim about arbitrary non-Pauli observables is made.
patches.units: Dimensionless finite-qubit operator relations; n, r, and k are integer counts where used.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional n-qubit Pauli stabilizer code; each chosen generator is a signed Hermitian Pauli operator with g_i^2=I.
The generators commute and their generated group S excludes -I, so the simultaneous +1 eigenspace is nonzero.
This is the commuting-generator condition for an ordinary Pauli stabilizer, not the potentially noncommuting gauge generators of a subsystem code.
Commutation alone does not guarantee a nonempty +1 space: the additional exclusion of -I is essential.
variables: [g_i,g_j]=g_i g_j-g_j g_i: commutator; i,j label stabilizer generators.
patches.regime: Within the Pauli group, two elements either commute or anticommute. Anticommuting invertible generators cannot share a nonzero +1 eigenvector. This is not a general assertion that arbitrary noncommuting matrices cannot share eigenvectors; independence is relevant to counting constraints, not to commutation itself.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional n-qubit Pauli stabilizer code; each chosen generator is a signed Hermitian Pauli operator with g_i^2=I.

The displayed list contains r independent stabilizer generators; 0<=r<=n.
Each factor (I+g_i)/2 is the orthogonal projector onto its +1 eigenspace; mutual commutation makes their product an orthogonal projector.
variables: P: orthogonal projector onto the code space, with P^2=P=P^dagger.
I: identity on the 2^n-dimensional physical Hilbert space; r: independent-generator count.
patches.regime: Normalized derivation from the source, not a verbatim displayed equation: expanding the product gives P=2^(-r) sum_{g in S} g. Its rank is 2^(n-r). A redundant consistent generator leaves the projector valid, but raw list length must not be substituted for the independent rank in the dimension formula. The empty product for r=0 is I.

patches.regime: Finite binary Pauli stabilizer codes. The exclusion of -I prevents a zero code space. Redundant constraints must be removed when counting r; the relation is not a dimension formula for arbitrary commuting operators or subsystem gauge-generator lists.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional n-qubit Pauli stabilizer code; each chosen generator is a signed Hermitian Pauli operator with g_i^2=I.
The generators commute and their generated group S excludes -I, so the simultaneous +1 eigenspace is nonzero.
At least one logical qubit is encoded. X_L and Z_L are a complementary pair for the same logical qubit, chosen as Pauli representatives commuting with S and acting nontrivially on the code.

For toric/surface-code string representatives, the sign is determined by odd parity of shared physical qubits carrying anticommuting Pauli factors. A single transverse primal/dual crossing is the standard toric example, not an assertion about arbitrary drawn curves.
variables: X_L, Z_L: encoded Pauli X and Z for one chosen logical qubit; L is a logical label.
N(S)/S: logical Pauli classes, with overall phases handled consistently; multiplication by a stabilizer does not change the encoded action.
patches.regime: The same-logical-qubit pair anticommutes; a canonical choice on different logical qubits commutes. The algebraic relation holds beyond topological codes. Geometric crossing language applies only when the chosen code and physical string supports justify it; even overlap parity gives commutation.
